about: Prerequisite + encompassing graph for the course. prereqs = must be mastered before learning. key_prereqs = the prerequisites most directly used; remediated when this topic is failed. encompasses = {topic: weight 0-1}: practicing this topic implicitly practices that one (drives FIRe credit in tools/srs.py). kps = knowledge points, taught and quizzed one at a time. picture = the geometric/visual intuition that must be tested, not just the procedure.

modules.title: Foundations II - Proving an algorithm is correct
Foundations III - What the machine actually does

topics.title: Big-O as a growth rate
kps: Count basic operations as a function of n for a loop and a nested loop
Drop constants and lower-order terms, and say why they stop mattering as n grows
Rank growth classes 1, log n, n, n log n, n^2, 2^n, n! and estimate each at n = 10^5
Time vs extra space; the input itself does not count toward extra space
Map interview constraints to a target complexity (n <= 20, 10^3, 10^5, 10^9)
topics.picture: Plot the curves: past some n the steeper curve stays above forever, whatever the constants. The 10^8 ops/sec budget is a horizontal line; each class crosses it at a different n.

topics.title: Logarithms as repeated halving
kps: log2 n = how many times n can be halved before reaching 1
Why the base does not matter inside Big-O (change of base is a constant factor)
Height of a complete binary tree with n leaves is log2 n
Recognise log factors in code: a loop that multiplies or divides its variable by 2
topics.picture: A number line cut in half again and again; and a balanced tree whose levels double, so n leaves need only log n levels.

topics.title: Arithmetic and geometric sums
kps: 1 + 2 + ... + n = n(n+1)/2 and why that makes 'for i, for j < i' O(n^2)
1 + 2 + 4 + ... + 2^k = 2^(k+1) - 1: the last term is bigger than all earlier terms combined
Tell which of the two a loop is summing, from the code
topics.picture: Arithmetic: a staircase of bars filling half of an n-by-n square. Geometric: each bar is taller than every bar before it put together, so the whole sum is less than twice the last bar.

topics.title: Counting: subsets, permutations, combinations
kps: 2^n subsets: each element is in or out
n! orderings; n choose k selections, and why k! ordered picks collapse to one
Size of the output as a lower bound on running time
Estimate when 2^n or n! is feasible (n about 20 vs about 10)
topics.picture: A binary decision tree: each level decides one element, so level n has 2^n leaves. Permutations: a tree whose branching factor shrinks n, n-1, ..., 1.

topics.title: Loop invariants
kps: State a property that is true before every iteration
Prove it holds initially, is maintained by one iteration, and gives the answer at termination
Use an invariant to find the bug in a wrong loop (off-by-one, wrong update order)
Termination: a quantity that strictly decreases and is bounded below
topics.picture: The array split into a processed region, where the invariant holds, and an unprocessed region; each iteration moves the boundary by one.

topics.title: Induction and recursive correctness
kps: Base case + inductive step, and why together they cover every n
Strong induction: assume all smaller cases, as recursion does
The recursive leap of faith: trust the call on the smaller input, check the combine step
Find the missing or wrong base case in a recursive function
topics.picture: Dominoes: the base case knocks the first; the step guarantees each one knocks the next.

topics.title: Search-space elimination
kps: Frame the problem as a search space (all pairs (i, j) with i < j as an upper-triangular grid)
Brute force visits every cell; a clever algorithm deletes whole rows or columns per step
Prove a deletion is safe: every discarded candidate cannot be the answer
Show a wrong move (e.g. moving the taller line in Container With Most Water) with a counterexample
topics.picture: The n-by-n grid of pairs. In sorted two-sum, sum too small at (lo, hi) means every pair (lo, j <= hi) is too small too, so row lo is erased. Each step erases one row or one column, so n steps cover all n^2 cells.

topics.title: Monotone predicates
kps: A predicate over an ordered domain that flips false to true exactly once
Find the monotone predicate hidden in a min/max word problem (can we finish in speed k?)
What breaks when the predicate is not monotone: counterexample
First-true vs last-false framing
topics.picture: A row F F F F T T T: the answer is the boundary, and checking one cell tells you which side of the boundary you are on.

topics.title: Memory model: arrays, references, boxing
kps: An array is contiguous, so index i is at base + i*size: O(1) access
A linked node is a separate object reached through a pointer
Java boxing: Integer vs int, HashMap<Integer,Integer> memory and speed cost
Cache locality: why an array scan beats a pointer chase at the same Big-O
topics.picture: A row of adjacent boxes vs boxes scattered across memory joined by arrows; a cache line pulls in neighbours for free only in the first case.

topics.title: Amortized analysis
kps: Amortized cost = total cost of a sequence / number of operations (not an average over random inputs)
Doubling array: total copy cost for n appends is 1 + 2 + 4 + ... < 2n, so O(1) amortized
Growing by a constant k instead: total copy cost is about n^2/(2k), so O(n) amortized; prove it
Accounting/banker's view: overcharge cheap ops to prepay the expensive one
Recognise the 'each element enters and leaves at most once' argument (stacks, windows)
topics.picture: A bar chart of per-append cost: mostly 1s with tall spikes at powers of two. Flatten the spikes over the cheap bars before them and the area under the chart is at most 3 per bar.

topics.title: How a hash table works
kps: Hash function maps a key to a bucket index; equal keys must hash equally (equals/hashCode)
Collisions and chaining; load factor = entries / buckets
Resize at a load-factor threshold, and why that keeps O(1) expected via amortization
Expected vs worst case: adversarial keys, Java 8 treeified buckets
When an array beats a map: small bounded key range (e.g. 26 letters)
topics.picture: A row of buckets with short chains hanging off them; when the average chain passes the threshold, double the row and redistribute.

topics.title: Tree anatomy
kps: Nodes, edges = n - 1, depth, height
Balanced height log n vs skewed height n: same n, different shape
Complete binary tree stored in an array: children at 2i+1 and 2i+2
BST ordering property and what it lets you skip
topics.picture: The same 7 values drawn as a bushy tree of height 3 and as a vine of height 7.

topics.title: Graph representation
kps: Vertices, edges, directed vs undirected, weighted
Adjacency list vs matrix: space V+E vs V^2, and when each wins
Why a full traversal is O(V + E), not O(V * E)
Grids as implicit graphs
topics.picture: Each edge gets looked at a constant number of times: sum of degrees = 2E.

topics.title: Recursion and the call stack
kps: Each call is a stack frame; the frame holds locals and a return point
Space = maximum depth of the call stack, not the total number of calls
Trace a recursion as a tree of calls
Stack overflow at depth about 10^4 in Java; when to convert to iteration
topics.picture: The recursion tree traversed depth-first; the live stack is only the path from root to the current node.

topics.title: Recurrences via recursion trees
kps: T(n) = T(n/2) + 1: one path of log n levels, so log n
T(n) = 2T(n/2) + n: log n levels of n work each, so n log n
T(n) = 2T(n-1) + 1: doubling levels, so 2^n (geometric sum dominated by the last level)
Work per level x number of levels; notice when one level dominates
topics.picture: Draw the tree and write the work done at each level down the right-hand side; add up the column.

topics.title: Sorting cost and the n log n lower bound
kps: Merge sort as T(n) = 2T(n/2) + n
A comparison sort is a decision tree with n! leaves; its height is at least log(n!), about n log n
Counting sort beats n log n by not comparing, and needs a bounded key range
When sorting destroys information you need (original indices)
topics.picture: A binary decision tree that must have a leaf for each of the n! orderings, so it cannot be shallower than log2(n!).

topics.title: Hash map pattern: complement lookup and counting
kps: Trade space for time: remember what you have seen
Complement lookup (two-sum) and why one pass suffices
Frequency maps and grouping by a canonical key (anagrams)
Prefix sums + hash map for subarray-sum = k
topics.picture: Walking left to right with a notebook: every earlier element is one O(1) lookup away.

topics.title: Converging two pointers
kps: Sorted two-sum and its elimination proof
3Sum: fix one index, converge on the rest; dedup without losing answers
Container With Most Water: why the shorter line is the one to move
Palindrome scans
topics.picture: The pair grid from F09, with the pointers walking a staircase path from the top-right corner.

topics.title: Same-direction pointers (read/write, fast/slow)
kps: Invariant: nums[0..slow) is the kept output so far
In-place dedup / remove element / move zeros
Merging two sorted sequences
topics.picture: Two arrows moving right: everything left of slow is finished output, everything between slow and fast is garbage.

topics.title: Sliding window
kps: Fixed window: add the entering element, remove the leaving one
Variable window: grow right, shrink left while the window is invalid
Why it is O(n): each index enters once and leaves once (amortized)
When windows fail: negative numbers break the 'shrinking only helps' property
topics.picture: A caterpillar crawling along the array: the head and tail only ever move right, so together they take at most 2n steps.

topics.title: Binary search on a sorted array
kps: Loop invariant for lo/hi (answer is in [lo, hi])
lo < hi vs lo <= hi, and mid rounding that avoids infinite loops
Lower bound / upper bound / first true
Rotated sorted array: which half is sorted?
topics.picture: The interval [lo, hi] on a number line halves each step, and the invariant says the answer never leaves it.

topics.title: Binary search on the answer space
kps: Spot 'minimise the maximum' / 'smallest k such that'
Write the feasibility check and prove it is monotone
Complexity = log(range) x cost of the check
topics.picture: The F13 boolean row, but the domain is candidate answers, not array positions.

topics.title: Stacks and monotonic stack
kps: LIFO matching (parentheses) and why a stack is the right shape
Monotonic stack invariant: the stack stays sorted
Next greater element: what a pop means
O(n) total despite the inner while loop (amortized)
topics.picture: Bars of different heights: a new tall bar hides every shorter bar to its left, which is exactly what gets popped.

topics.title: Linked-list manipulation
kps: Dummy head node and why it removes edge cases
In-place reversal: three pointers and the order of assignments
Floyd cycle detection and why fast catches slow
Finding the middle / k-th from the end
topics.picture: Draw boxes and arrows; rewire one arrow at a time and check nothing gets orphaned.

topics.title: Tree DFS and BFS
kps: Recursive DFS: define what the function returns for a subtree
Top-down (pass state down) vs bottom-up (return info up)
BFS by levels with a queue
BST problems using the ordering property; validate BST with bounds
topics.picture: Each subtree is a smaller copy of the problem; the answer at a node is combined from its children's answers.

topics.title: Heaps and top-K
kps: Heap property and sift up/down in O(log n)
Top-K with a size-k min-heap: why a min-heap for the largest K
Merge K sorted lists
Two heaps for a running median
topics.picture: A complete tree where every parent beats its children; the size-k min-heap is a bouncer that evicts the weakest of the current top k.

topics.title: Backtracking
kps: Choose / explore / un-choose
Subsets, permutations, combinations as decision trees
Pruning: cut a branch as soon as it cannot lead to a valid answer
Complexity from the size of the decision tree
topics.picture: The F14 decision tree, walked depth-first, with dead branches cut off.

topics.title: Graph BFS/DFS and connected components
kps: Visited set: why trees do not need one and graphs do
BFS gives shortest paths in unweighted graphs: proof by layers
Grid flood fill / number of islands
Multi-source BFS
topics.picture: BFS as ripples in a pond: layer d is exactly the set of nodes at distance d.

topics.title: Topological sort
kps: Kahn's algorithm: repeatedly remove in-degree-0 nodes
Cycle detection when nodes remain
DFS post-order reversed
topics.picture: Peel off nodes with no incoming arrows, layer by layer.

topics.title: Dijkstra
kps: Greedy settle-the-closest and why non-negative weights make it safe
Lazy deletion with a PriorityQueue
Counterexample with a negative edge
topics.picture: A growing ball of settled nodes; the frontier node closest to the source can never later be reached more cheaply.

topics.title: Union-find
kps: Parent pointers forming a forest
Path compression and union by rank; near-constant amortized cost
When to use it instead of BFS (incremental connectivity)
topics.picture: Trees of people pointing to their group leader; compression flattens the trees.

topics.title: Dynamic programming
kps: Overlapping subproblems: spot repeated nodes in the recursion tree
State definition: what exactly does dp[i] mean, in words
Recurrence from the last decision; prove it by induction
Memoization vs tabulation and fill order
Complexity = number of states x work per state
DP vs greedy: when a local choice can be wrong (counterexample)
topics.picture: The exponential recursion tree collapses into a small DAG once identical subtrees are merged.

topics.title: Intervals and greedy
kps: Sort by start to merge; sort by end to schedule the most intervals
Exchange argument: swap an optimal solution's first choice for the greedy one without losing
Sweep line / meeting rooms with a heap
Counterexample for the wrong sort key
topics.picture: Intervals as segments on a timeline; the greedy choice leaves the most room to the right.
